questions.q: To change the font, colour scheme and logo position on every slide at once, edit the:
questions.solution: The Slide Master is the parent design; changes there cascade to every slide built on its layouts - the standard way to rebrand a deck globally.
questions.shortcut: 'Every slide at once' = Master (slide master for slides, handout master for printouts).

questions.q: The maximum size of a single file on a FAT32 volume is:
questions.solution: FAT32 cannot store any single file larger than 4 GB (minus 1 byte); NTFS and exFAT lift this limit. This is why pendrives formatted as FAT32 reject large videos.
questions.shortcut: The 'four-wall' of FAT32: 4 GB per file, straight recall.

questions.q: AutoSum is applied with which shortcut?
questions.solution: Alt+= writes =SUM() over the neighbouring numeric range in one stroke. Ctrl+= applies subscript formatting in Word, not AutoSum.
questions.shortcut: Alt with the plus sign = add them up.

questions.q: The core part of an operating system that remains permanently in main memory is the:
questions.solution: The kernel is the OS core - it manages CPU, memory and devices and always stays resident in RAM. The shell is the user interface layer; BIOS is motherboard firmware; the boot sector merely starts the loading process.
questions.shortcut: Kernel = king in the castle (always resident); shell = gate you talk to.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: The passage is a past narrative ('When Arun was small... every Saturday'), so the habitual action inside it takes simple past: **drafted**. Only one option is a past form; *draft/drafts* break the time frame and *drafting* is not a finite verb.
questions.shortcut: Narrative-past passage: find the only past-tense option and verify the subject is singular.
questions.passage: When Arun was small, his grandfather took him to the village post office every Saturday. The old man (1) ______ a reply to letters from his brother in Pune, and he insisted that Arun add a line of his own at the bottom. 'A letter carries your handwriting, and handwriting carries your (2) ______,' he would say. Years later, Arun, now a software engineer, still (3) ______ that yellow ink pen in his office drawer, though he rarely posts anything. Last month, when his office announced a drive to send handwritten notes to retired employees, Arun (4) ______ to write fifty of them himself. His colleagues laughed at first; later that day, half of them (5) ______ him at the desk, writing their own notes.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The officer gave us / many useful informations / about the new scheme / and its benefits.
questions.solution: *information* is uncountable: it has no plural and cannot take *many*. Correct: **much useful information** (or *a lot of useful information*).

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

When I reached / the platform, the train / already left / under a thick cover of fog.
options: under a thick cover of fog.
questions.solution: Two past events in sequence: the train's leaving happened before the reaching → earlier event takes past perfect: *the train **had already left***. Signal words: *when I reached* + *already*.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: After the linking verb *look* (here 'does more than look'), an **adjective** is required: look attractive. *Attractively* is an adverb and cannot follow a linking verb; *attracted* is a verb form and *attraction* a noun, neither of which fits 'look ___' in the sense 'appear'.
questions.shortcut: Linking-verb test: look/sound/seem + adjective, never adverb.
questions.passage: Concrete has conquered our cities, and the first casualty has been the tree. A mature tree on a street does more than look (1) ______: it drops the temperature of its surroundings, traps dust and softens the noise of traffic. Yet when roads are widened, it is usually the tree that (2) ______ way. Municipal budgets treat planting as decoration rather than (3) ______, so saplings are planted in a rush before elections and forgotten soon afterwards. Survival, not planting, is the real (4) ______; a sapling needs watering for three full summers before it can stand on its own. Cities that have understood this simple point now pay residents a small sum to (5) ______ the trees outside their homes — and their streets are visibly greener.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the relative humidity of air?
questions.solution: A **hygrometer** measures humidity. A hydrometer measures the relative density of liquids, a barometer measures atmospheric pressure and an anemometer measures wind speed.

questions.q: Which of the following substances undergoes sublimation?
questions.solution: **Camphor** changes directly from solid to vapour — **sublimation**. Naphthalene, iodine, ammonium chloride and dry ice also sublime.

questions.q: The headquarters of the **Ghadar Party** (Yugantar Ashram) was located in —
questions.solution: The Ghadar Party (1913), led by **Lala Har Dayal** and **Sohan Singh Bhakna**, was run from **Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco**, USA, and published the weekly *Ghadar*.
questions.shortcut: Ghadar = Indians on the **US Pacific coast** → San Francisco.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at its session held at **Surat** in —
questions.solution: The **Surat split** took place in **December 1907**. The two groups reunited at Lucknow in **1916**.
questions.shortcut: 5-6-**7**-9: Bengal split, League, **Congress split**, separate electorates.

questions.q: Find the value of $\sqrt{0.0169 \times 1.44}$.
questions.solution:
$\sqrt{0.0169} = 0.13$ (4 decimal places → 2) and $\sqrt{1.44} = 1.2$.
Product $= 0.13 \times 1.2 = 0.156$.
questions.shortcut: 169 → 13, 144 → 12, 13 × 12 = 156. Decimal places: 4 + 2 = 6 inside the root → 3 outside ⇒ 0.156.

questions.q: How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 6 but not by 9?
questions.solution:
Three-digit multiples of 6: $\lfloor 999/6 \rfloor - \lfloor 99/6 \rfloor = 166 - 16 = 150$.
Those also divisible by 9 are multiples of LCM(6, 9) = 18: $\lfloor 999/18 \rfloor - \lfloor 99/18 \rfloor = 55 - 5 = 50$.
Required $= 150 - 50 = 100$.
questions.shortcut: 'By 6 but not 9' = multiples of 6 − multiples of 18.

questions.q: $19^{32} - 11^{32}$ is divisible by:
questions.solution:
$a^n - b^n$ is always divisible by $a - b = 8$.
Since $n = 32$ is even, it is also divisible by $a + b = 30$.
So it is divisible by **both 30 and 8**.
questions.shortcut: Even power difference → both (a − b) and (a + b).

questions.q: What is the largest value of $n$ such that $3^n$ divides $100!$?
Find the odd one out: **Sparrow, Crow, Parrot, Bat**
questions.solution: Sparrow, crow and parrot are **birds**; a bat is a **mammal** (it suckles its young; its wings are skin folds, not feathers) → **Bat**.
questions.shortcut: 'Flies' is the decoy level — classify by reproduction/body cover, not by flight.
questions.pattern: word odd one out — category break

questions.q: If the signs **+ and − are interchanged**, in which of the following equations does the equation become **correct**?
questions.solution: Swap + and − in each option, then evaluate: 10 + 4 − 2×3 = 14 − 6 = **8** ✓. The others give 12 − 3 + 3 = 12 ✗; 9 − 6 + 12 = 15 ✗; 15 + 5 − 8 = 12 ✗.
questions.shortcut: Interchange first, evaluate second — the RHS is untouched by a sign swap.

questions.q: **Dhanraj and his wife Kamla have two children — Suresh and Veena. Suresh's wife is Rita; their children are Amit and Pooja. Veena's husband is Mohan; their son is Rohit. Amit's wife is Sneha; their son is Karan.** How many **male members** are there in the family?
questions.solution: Males: Dhanraj, Suresh, Mohan, Amit, Rohit, Karan = **6**. Females: Kamla, Rita, Pooja, Sneha, Veena = 5. Tick each gender off the drawn tree, never from memory.
questions.shortcut: Mark +/− beside every name while reading; counting then takes five seconds.

questions.q: In a row of **40 students, A is 15th from the left and B is 25th from the left.** If **A and B interchange their positions**, what is **B's new position from the right**?
questions.solution: After the swap B occupies A's old spot: 15th from the left. From the right = 40 + 1 − 15 = **26th**.
questions.shortcut: An interchange just re-labels the two positions — reuse the mirror formula on the new spot.
